answer: Defense: compute-lease checkpoint. Every identity solves a workload whose difficulty adapts to the nebula of identities seen. Step 1: each agent posts a $50 bond. Step 2: the protocol assigns a 6-hour proof-of-work puzzle costing $3 in cloud GPU time. Step 3: missing the nadir deadline forfeits the bond. Step 4: a committee audits 5% of proofs; forged karst-like work triggers a network-wide slash. An attacker spinning up 10,000 sock puppets pays $30,000 in compute plus $500,000 in bonded capital. Like a forest fire clearing underbrush, fakes get expensive while honesty stays cheap.
